newsitem.title: UK: Mercury lifts first half pretax profits 29 percent.
newsitem.headline: Mercury lifts first half pretax profits 29 percent.

text.p: British fund management company Mercury Asset Management on Tuesday announced a 29 percent jump in first half pretax profits to 81.8 million pounds compared to 63.6 million pounds in the first half last year.

Mercury, formerly controlled by S.G. Warburg before the latter was bought by Swiss Bank Corp last year, raised its interim dividend to 10 pence per share from six pence last time and said the significant increase was due to a rebalancing betrween interim and final payouts.
Funds under management rose to 85.9 billion pounds at the end of September after 70.9 billion at the same time last year. The most recent figure includes two billion pounds of net new business.
MAM said it had seen a rise in defined contribution pension schem business in the last six months and expects this to be a growth area.

MAM chairman Hugh Stevenson said the course of equity markets will determine the company's full year results, adding it is determined to maintain its record of creating shareholder value through profitable expasion.
